rationale: These are finite resource allocations, not measured durations or completion guarantees. The companion runtime-policy.html explains their scope and limitations.

control.rationale: Metadata, matrix construction, drift checks, result aggregation and deployment receive ten minutes for setup and primary work plus five minutes for variation. These jobs do not receive the dependency-heavy test allowance.

standard.rationale: Dependency-heavy tests and documentation builds receive fifteen minutes for setup, thirty for primary work and fifteen for variation. The resulting cap is a resource ceiling; cold-cache completion within it remains unverified.

publication.rationale: Publication runs the unsharded test command before build and upload. Its serial test allocation is larger than a domain shard allocation. Thirty additional minutes permit variation within a finite cap. No publication duration is inferred from aggregate shard time; successful publication within this cap remains unverified.

retained_focused.rationale: The existing focused-test limit is retained without a new runtime estimate or added margin.

retained_sweep.rationale: The existing per-shard full-sweep limit is retained without a new runtime estimate or added margin.

baseline_freshness.rationale: A daily full sweep plus a six-hour grace window permits scheduling and completion variation of one quarter of the daily cadence without accepting an entirely missed daily sweep. This is a staleness tolerance, not a claim about hosted scheduling. Selection uses run updated_at; comparison also checks shard completed_at. Future evidence and ages beyond the inclusive window are rejected.
